page.title: Η επικοινωνία μεταξύ ιατρού και ασθενούς κατά τη διάρκεια μίας ιατρικής επίσκεψης από την πλευρά του ασθενούς
page.attribution: apothesis; Η επικοινωνία μεταξύ ιατρού και ασθενούς κατά τη διάρκεια μίας ιατρικής επίσκεψης από την πλευρά του ασθενούς

docai_lines.text: ABSTRACT
Introduction: In recent years, the development of technology has contributed significantly
to the elimination of certain diseases and viruses. However, about HIV / AIDS, it has not
yet been found the treatment, as a result to increasing the rate of morbidity and mortality in
patients.
Purpose: The purpose of this study was to investigate the knowledge and attitudes of
nurses towards people with HIV / AIDS.
Materials and Methods: The search was performed on the PUBMED and CINAHL
electronic databases. The research articles were published between 2009-2019. During the
search 200 articles were initially selected and eventually through some criteria and
deficiencies I concluded only 9 articles.
Results: Through the search of bibliography revealed that there are a large number of
nurses who have negative attitudes towards HIV/AIDS patients. At the same time, it
appeared that in some studies nurses had a low or moderate level of knowledge about
AIDS and therefore needed more education. However, it has been found that there is a
respectable percentage of nurses who have sufficient knowledge of HIV and at the same
time maintain a positive attitude towards these patients.
Conclusion: The knowledge and attitudes of nurses play a key role in the care and
convalescence of these patients. Studies have shown that there are nurses who have
insufficient knowledge about the HIV/AIDS virus and this has led to negative management
of patients. So these nurses need to be identified and the authorities need to push them to
follow the guidelines, to have a continuous education and instruction in contemporary data
to care for this group of patients. Even HIV-positive patients need to be treated equally and
not be marginalized.
Keywords: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, Human Immunodeficiency Virus,
Nursing Knowledge, Nursing Attitudes
